```{r}

install.packages("gridExtra")

# LOAD PACKAGES

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(AER)
library(scales)
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)


# FUNCTION FOR WHITE VISUAL TABLES

show_table <- function(data, title) {

  table_theme <- ttheme_minimal(
    base_size = 11,

    core = list(
      bg_params = list(
        fill = "white",
        col = "grey80"
      ),
      fg_params = list(
        col = "black"
      )
    ),

    colhead = list(
      bg_params = list(
        fill = "white",
        col = "grey70"
      ),
      fg_params = list(
        col = "black",
        fontface = "bold"
      )
    )
  )

  table_plot <- tableGrob(
    data,
    rows = NULL,
    theme = table_theme
  )

  title_plot <- textGrob(
    title,
    gp = gpar(
      fontsize = 16,
      fontface = "bold",
      col = "black"
    )
  )

  final_table <- arrangeGrob(
    title_plot,
    table_plot,
    ncol = 1,
    heights = c(0.12, 0.88)
  )

  grid.newpage()

  grid.draw(
    rectGrob(
      gp = gpar(
        fill = "white",
        col = "white"
      )
    )
  )

  grid.draw(final_table)
}


# LOAD DATA
# Select d_HHP2020_241.Rdata

load(file.choose())


# CREATE PRIME-AGE SAMPLE

prime_age_laborforce_data <- d_HHP2020_24 %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(work_kind),
    Age >= 25,
    Age <= 55,
    income_midpoint > 0
  )


# CREATE AGE GROUPS

prime_age_laborforce_data <- prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  mutate(
    Age_Group = case_when(
      Age >= 25 & Age <= 34 ~ "25-34",
      Age >= 35 & Age <= 44 ~ "35-44",
      Age >= 45 & Age <= 55 ~ "45-55"
    )
  )


# TABLE 1: OVERALL INCOME STATISTICS

overall_income_statistics <- data.frame(

  Statistic = c(
    "Number of Observations",
    "Mean Income",
    "Median Income",
    "Standard Deviation",
    "Minimum Income",
    "Maximum Income"
  ),

  Value = c(

    nrow(prime_age_laborforce_data),

    mean(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    median(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    sd(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    min(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    max(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
)

overall_income_statistics$Value <-
  round(
    overall_income_statistics$Value,
    2
  )

show_table(
  overall_income_statistics,
  "Table 1: Overall Income Statistics"
)


# TABLE 2: INCOME STATISTICS BY RACE

mean_income_race <- prime_age_laborforce_data %>%
  group_by(Race) %>%
  summarise(

    Mean_Income = mean(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Median_Income = median(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    SD_Income = sd(
      income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    N = n(),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

race_table_display <- mean_income_race %>%
  mutate(

    Mean_Income = dollar(
      Mean_Income,
      accuracy = 1
    ),

    Median_Income = dollar(
      Median_Income,
      accuracy = 1
    ),

    SD_Income = dollar(
      SD_Income,
      accuracy = 1
    )
  )

show_table(
  race_table_display,
  "Table 2: Income Statistics by Race"
)


# GRAPH: MEAN INCOME BY RACE

ggplot(
  mean_income_race,
  aes(
    x = Race,
    y = Mean_Income,
    fill = Race
  )
) +

  geom_col(
    width = 0.7,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = dollar(
        Mean_Income,
        accuracy = 1
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.12)
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Mean Income by Race",
    subtitle = "Prime-Age Workers, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Race",
    y = "Mean Income"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# MAIN REGRESSION

model_1 <- lm(

  income_midpoint ~

    Age +

    Gender +

    Education +

    Race +

    Hispanic,

  data = prime_age_laborforce_data
)


# TABLE 7: MAIN REGRESSION RESULTS

regression_results <-
  summary(model_1)$coefficients

confidence_intervals <-
  confint(model_1)

regression_table <- data.frame(

  Variable =
    rownames(regression_results),

  Coefficient =
    regression_results[, 1],

  Standard_Error =
    regression_results[, 2],

  T_Statistic =
    regression_results[, 3],

  P_Value =
    regression_results[, 4],

  CI_Lower =
    confidence_intervals[, 1],

  CI_Upper =
    confidence_intervals[, 2],

  row.names = NULL
)

regression_table <- regression_table %>%
  mutate(

    Coefficient = round(
      Coefficient,
      2
    ),

    Standard_Error = round(
      Standard_Error,
      2
    ),

    T_Statistic = round(
      T_Statistic,
      2
    ),

    P_Value = round(
      P_Value,
      4
    ),

    CI_Lower = round(
      CI_Lower,
      2
    ),

    CI_Upper = round(
      CI_Upper,
      2
    )
  )

regression_table_display <- regression_table

names(regression_table_display) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Coefficient",
  "Std. Error",
  "t-stat",
  "p-value",
  "95% CI Lower",
  "95% CI Upper"
)

show_table(
  regression_table_display,
  "Table 7: Main Regression Results"
)


# TABLE 8: ROBUST STANDARD ERRORS

robust_results <- coeftest(

  model_1,

  vcov = vcovHC(
    model_1,
    type = "HC1"
  )
)

robust_table <- data.frame(

  Variable =
    rownames(robust_results),

  Coefficient =
    robust_results[, 1],

  Robust_SE =
    robust_results[, 2],

  T_Statistic =
    robust_results[, 3],

  P_Value =
    robust_results[, 4],

  row.names = NULL
)

robust_table <- robust_table %>%
  mutate(

    Coefficient = round(
      Coefficient,
      2
    ),

    Robust_SE = round(
      Robust_SE,
      2
    ),

    T_Statistic = round(
      T_Statistic,
      2
    ),

    P_Value = round(
      P_Value,
      4
    )
  )

robust_table_display <- robust_table

names(robust_table_display) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Coefficient",
  "Robust SE",
  "t-stat",
  "p-value"
)

show_table(
  robust_table_display,
  "Table 8: Regression Results with Robust Standard Errors"
)


# TABLE 9: OVERALL REGRESSION MODEL STATISTICS

model_statistics <- data.frame(

  Statistic = c(
    "Number of Observations",
    "R-Squared",
    "Adjusted R-Squared",
    "Residual Standard Error"
  ),

  Value = c(

    nobs(model_1),

    summary(model_1)$r.squared,

    summary(model_1)$adj.r.squared,

    sigma(model_1)
  )
)

model_statistics$Value <-
  round(
    model_statistics$Value,
    4
  )

show_table(
  model_statistics,
  "Table 9: Overall Regression Model Statistics"
)


# PREDICTED INCOME

to_be_predicted1 <- data.frame(

  Age = 25:55,

  Gender = "female",

  Education = "adv degree",

  Race = "Black",

  Hispanic = "Hispanic"
)

to_be_predicted1$yhat <- predict(
  model_1,
  newdata = to_be_predicted1
)


to_be_predicted2 <- data.frame(

  Age = 25:55,

  Gender = "female",

  Education = "high school",

  Race = "Black",

  Hispanic = "Hispanic"
)

to_be_predicted2$yhat <- predict(
  model_1,
  newdata = to_be_predicted2
)


prediction_data <- rbind(

  data.frame(
    Age = to_be_predicted1$Age,
    Predicted_Income = to_be_predicted1$yhat,
    Education = "Advanced Degree"
  ),

  data.frame(
    Age = to_be_predicted2$Age,
    Predicted_Income = to_be_predicted2$yhat,
    Education = "High School"
  )
)


# GRAPH: PREDICTED INCOME BY AGE AND EDUCATION

ggplot(
  prediction_data,
  aes(
    x = Age,
    y = Predicted_Income,
    color = Education,
    linetype = Education
  )
) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format()
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Predicted Income by Age and Education",
    subtitle = "Black Hispanic Female, Ages 25-55",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Predicted Income",
    color = "Education",
    linetype = "Education"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# LOG-INCOME MODEL

model_log <- lm(

  log(income_midpoint) ~

    Age +

    Gender +

    Education +

    Race +

    Hispanic,

  data = prime_age_laborforce_data
)


# TABLE 10: LOG-INCOME REGRESSION RESULTS

log_results <-
  summary(model_log)$coefficients

log_table <- data.frame(

  Variable =
    rownames(log_results),

  Coefficient =
    log_results[, 1],

  Standard_Error =
    log_results[, 2],

  T_Statistic =
    log_results[, 3],

  P_Value =
    log_results[, 4],

  row.names = NULL
)

log_table <- log_table %>%
  mutate(

    Coefficient = round(
      Coefficient,
      4
    ),

    Standard_Error = round(
      Standard_Error,
      4
    ),

    T_Statistic = round(
      T_Statistic,
      2
    ),

    P_Value = round(
      P_Value,
      4
    )
  )

log_table_display <- log_table

names(log_table_display) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Coefficient",
  "Std. Error",
  "t-stat",
  "p-value"
)

show_table(
  log_table_display,
  "Table 10: Log-Income Regression Results"
)


# TABLE 11: ACTUAL AND PREDICTED MEAN INCOME

predicted_level <-
  predict(model_1)

predicted_log <-
  predict(model_log)

predicted_log_income <-
  exp(predicted_log)

comparison <- data.frame(

  Measure = c(
    "Actual Mean Income",
    "Mean Predicted Income - Level Model",
    "Mean Predicted Income - Log Model"
  ),

  Mean_Income = c(

    mean(
      prime_age_laborforce_data$income_midpoint,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    mean(
      predicted_level,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    mean(
      predicted_log_income,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
)

comparison$Mean_Income <-
  dollar(
    comparison$Mean_Income,
    accuracy = 1
  )

show_table(
  comparison,
  "Table 11: Actual and Predicted Mean Income"
)


# AGE-SQUARED MODEL

model_age_squared <- lm(

  income_midpoint ~

    Age +

    I(Age^2) +

    Gender +

    Education +

    Race +

    Hispanic,

  data = prime_age_laborforce_data
)


# TABLE 12: AGE-SQUARED REGRESSION RESULTS

age_squared_results <-
  summary(model_age_squared)$coefficients

age_squared_table <- data.frame(

  Variable =
    rownames(age_squared_results),

  Coefficient =
    age_squared_results[, 1],

  Standard_Error =

  T_Statistic =
    age_squared_results[, 3],

    age_squared_results[, 4],

  row.names = NULL

age_squared_table <- age_squared_table %>%
  mutate(

    Coefficient = round(
      Coefficient,
      2
    ),

    Standard_Error = round(
      Standard_Error,
      2
    ),

    T_Statistic = round(
      T_Statistic,
      2
    ),

    P_Value = round(
      P_Value,
      4
    )
  )

age_squared_table_display <-
  age_squared_table

names(age_squared_table_display) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Coefficient",
  "Std. Error",
  "t-stat",

show_table(
```
